kf: Glucocorticoid excess: **iatrogenic** (steroids) is far commoner than endogenous Cushing's.
Skin signs: **thin skin, wide purple striae, easy bruising**, acne, hirsutism, plethora, poor wound healing, fungal infections.
Body habitus: moon face, dorsocervical and supraclavicular fat pads, proximal myopathy.
Iatrogenic: **never stop steroids abruptly**; taper, Steroid Emergency Card and sick-day rules.
Endogenous: refer to endocrinology, urgently with hypokalaemia, severe hypertension or rapid progression.
myths: **"Striae always mean Cushing's"**: pale narrow striae are common; wide (>1 cm) purple striae are the concern.
patho_lead: Excess cortisol **breaks down collagen and protein**, thinning skin and vessels.

mech.t: Cortisol inhibits fibroblasts and collagen synthesis.
Dermis thins; stretching tears it into wide purple striae.
Adrenal androgens cause acne and hirsutism; immunosuppression allows fungal infection.

comp: Diabetes, hypertension, osteoporosis, VTE, infection, mood disorder.
prog: Skin signs improve as cortisol normalises.
